title: Two in a row

brief.story: The bike light needs two red LEDs, one after the other, on the 9 V pack. Both LEDs and their wiring are in; the one resistor that feeds them isn’t.
brief.goal: Fit one resistor so both LEDs carry 12–20 mA.

hints: One resistor feeds both LEDs: it goes from column 3 (the + feed) to column 8, where LED1’s long leg is.
In series the same current flows through everything, and the voltages add up: the two LEDs take 2.0 V each, so the resistor gets 9 − 2 − 2 = 5 V.
R = 5 V ÷ 15 mA ≈ 330 Ω (15.2 mA). 270 Ω or 390 Ω work too.

spec.explain: Both LEDs share one current: the resistor gets what the two LEDs leave, 9 − 2 − 2 = 5 V.

debrief: Two LEDs in a line share one current, and their voltages stack: 2 V + 2 V, leaving 5 V for the resistor. That’s why LED strips run from 12 V in groups of three: three LEDs take about 9 V and a small resistor takes the rest, so almost nothing is wasted as heat.
